name: Flighty Pro
subcategory: trip planning, navigation and travel intelligence
tagline: Organize booked flights and display user-entered status updates offline

pricing.notes: Annual Pro price divided by 12; monthly and lifetime options may exist.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited flight tracking; past-flight import limited to 365 days; first tracked flight includes core Pro features
tiers.notes: The complimentary first flight does not include Calendar Import, Email Forwarding, or TripIt Import.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited flights and history, email/calendar/TripIt import, full airport data, and 65+ flight-alert types
tiers.notes: $59.99 billed annually; the website displays $4.99/month as the annual-plan equivalent.

tiers.name: Pay-As-You-Go
tiers.limits: One non-recurring Pro purchase; exact entitlement duration is not stated on the public pricing page

tiers.name: Family
tiers.limits: Up to 6 family members through Apple Family Sharing
tiers.notes: $119 billed annually; all members generally need compatible Apple Family Sharing regions.

tiers.name: Lifetime
tiers.notes: $299 one-time. Previous annual payments are not automatically credited toward Lifetime.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free plan: unlimited tracked flights and live flight data, 365 days of past-flight import, and 1 complimentary Pro flight; 0 ongoing push alerts, delay predictions, Live Activities, or automatic calendar/email/TripIt sync after that flight.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly ($9.99), annual ($59.99), one-time Pay-As-You-Go ($4.99), Family monthly/annual, or individual Lifetime ($299)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Apple handles billing and refunds. Annual-to-Lifetime payments are not automatically credited. Family Lifetime ($449) still appears in App Store purchase listings, but Flighty's current help center says it is no longer sold.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Flighty Pro, organize booked flights and display user-entered status updates offline. The hard boundary is live aviation data, predictive alerts, apple integration, push infrastructure, and polish, plus proprietary live data and network coverage.
coreLoopDIY: Organize booked flights and user-entered status updates, map user-entered places and reservations, and keep an offline itinerary without claiming live proprietary availability.
requirements: optional public transit or weather API
whatYouLose: live aviation data, predictive alerts, Apple integration, push infrastructure, and polish
booking, disruption support, and offline map fleet
moatNotes: proprietary live data and network coverage
ongoingBurden: map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Flighty Pro because travel subscriptions sell current data and confidence during disruption, not just an itinerary list. The recurring cost buys map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Wanderer
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted trail database and route explorer using open map data.

alternatives.name: KDE Itinerary
alternatives.desc: It reads reservations locally and tracks the journey; Android and Linux only.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal itinerary organizer DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Flighty Pro in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, MapLibre GL, and user-supplied map and travel APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize booked flights and user-entered status updates, map user-entered places and reservations, and keep an offline itinerary without claiming live proprietary availability.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create trips, days, places, reservations, notes, documents, packing items, and emergency contacts.
Geocode only user-entered places and display them through MapLibre with cached trip-area tiles where allowed.
Parse forwarded reservation text locally into editable fields without logging message content.
Build a day timeline, route overview, conflict warnings, timezone display, and offline printable itinerary.
Allow manual updates for delays and reservations and label all external data with source and timestamp.
Export a complete trip bundle as JSON, calendar file, Markdown, and PDF.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out live flight, hotel, award, or ticket inventory.
Deliberately leave out commercial turn-by-turn navigation and global offline maps.
Deliberately leave out booking guarantees, disruption rebooking, and traveler support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
